task: All facts below are synthetic. Draft a 150–190-word JACS abstract emphasizing the contribution of a hierarchical reaction-structure method. It predicts a continuous bonding graph from mapped endpoint graphs, samples coordinates under that graph, and validates paths on a potential surface. Small-set benchmark: 120 reactions, bond-order MAE 0.041; with predicted graphs, the median per-reaction lowest TS RMSD among 12 retained candidates is 0.18 Å before refinement; 111/120 reactions obtain a frequency-characterized, endpoint-verified IRC path; on those 111 reactions the reference-assisted lowest post-refinement RMSD median is 0.07 Å. Larger cycloaddition set: 72/80 reactions succeed at the same budget; selecting the successful candidate closest to the reference barrier gives MAE 2.6 kcal mol−1 and Spearman rho 0.91. No experimental-rate or cross-family-transfer evidence is supplied. Return only the abstract.

Rewrite the following synthetic Results notes as one persuasive English paragraph of 90–130 words, explaining the method's design and removing a technical-audit tone. Graph-conditioned Model A samples coordinates with a fixed bonding hypothesis; changing hypotheses explores a different bonding state. Model B uses endpoint graphs alone and has a different architecture. On the same reaction set with equal sampling budgets, A has a median within-reaction pairwise RMSD of 0.21 Å and B 0.58 Å. Under predicted hypotheses, representative selection retains accurate candidates with median reference-assisted lowest RMSD 0.16 Å. No component ablation is supplied. Avoid ending with a generic future-validation sentence. Return only the paragraph.
